title: A Suspension-Trapping Protocol for Bottom-Up Proteomics Sample Preparation
author: Joseph Schrader
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML

steps.title: Prepare lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 125 µL of 10 % SDS with 500 µL of 100 mM Tris (pH 8.5) to obtain 2 % SDS lysis buffer as described in the Recipes.

steps.title: Prepare DTT working solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 15.4 mg of DTT in 1 mL Milli‑Q water to make a 160 mM DTT working solution.

steps.title: Prepare IAA solution
steps.instruction: Add 36.98 mg of IAA (kept at 4 °C) to 1 mL Milli‑Q water to obtain a 360 mM IAA solution.

steps.title: Prepare 12 % phosphoric acid
steps.instruction: Mix 420 µL of 85 % H₃PO₄ stock with 2 580 µL Milli‑Q water to give a 12 % (v/v) phosphoric acid solution.

steps.title: Prepare S‑trap binding buffer
steps.instruction: Combine methanol and 1 M TEAB (pH 7.1) to obtain a buffer containing 90 % methanol and 1 M TEAB; rinse glassware with 100 % methanol before preparation.

steps.title: Prepare trypsin stock
steps.instruction: Resuspend trypsin in 50 mM Tris, pH 8.5, to a concentration of 1 mg mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Prepare elution buffer 1
steps.instruction: Mix equal volumes of 100 mM TEAB and Milli‑Q water to obtain 50 mM TEAB elution buffer.

steps.title: Prepare elution buffer 2
steps.instruction: Prepare a solution of 0.2 % (v/v) formic acid in water.

steps.title: Prepare elution buffer 3
steps.instruction: Mix 50 % (v/v) acetonitrile with water and add 0.2 % (v/v) formic acid.

steps.title: Prepare aqueous buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 47.5 % acetonitrile, 47.5 % water, and 5 % formic acid (v/v) as described in the Recipes.

steps.title: Top‑14 depletion (tube format)
steps.instruction: Deplete high‑abundance proteins from CSF using the High‑Select Top 14 spin column.

substeps.instruction: Equilibrate the depletion spin column to room temperature for at least 5 min.
Remove the screw cap from the column.
Add up to 80 µL of CSF sample directly to the resin slurry.
Cap the column securely and invert several times to homogenize the resin.
Incubate 10 min at room temperature with gentle end‑over‑end mixing (or vortex gently every 2–3 min; incubation may be extended to 20–30 min).
Snap off the bottom closure of the column.
Loosen the top cap, place the column into a 2 mL collection tube, and centrifuge at 1 000 × g for 2 min.
Discard the resin‑containing column; retain the filtrate (depleted sample).
Resuspend the filtrate in PBS (10 mM, pH 7.4) containing 0.02 % sodium azide; store at –20 °C or proceed.
Place the collection tube in an Eppendorf Vacufuge, set V‑AQ mode to 30 °C for 4 h to dry (alternatively dry at room temperature to avoid loss).

steps.title: Top‑14 depletion (plate format)
steps.instruction: Deplete high‑abundance proteins from CSF using a 96‑well plate format.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µL of High‑Select Top 14 resin to each well of a 0.8 mL 96‑well storage plate.
Add 40 µL of CSF sample to each well.
Seal the plate with a round‑top sealing mat.
Vortex the sealed plate moderately for 30 s.
Invert the plate several times, then vortex for 5 min.
Place the plate on a rotator and rotate for 20 min.
Pulse‑centrifuge the plate for 10–15 s (mat still on) to settle resin.
Remove the sealing mat.
Transfer the well contents to an AcroPrep 96‑well filter plate (0.2 µm) positioned above a 2 mL collection plate.
Add 200 µL of PBS (10 mM, pH 7.4) to each storage well, mix, and transfer the remaining resin to the filter plate.
Centrifuge at 8 000 × g for 5 min to collect flow‑through.
Place the collection plate in a SpeedVac concentrator to dry.

steps.title: Trypsin digestion (tube format)
steps.instruction: Perform reduction, alkylation, acidification, S‑Trap binding, and overnight trypsin digestion in tube format.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend each depleted sample in 175 µL of 1× lysis buffer (2 % SDS, 100 mM Tris, pH 8.5).
Add 25 µL of 160 mM DTT (prepared above) to reach 20 mM final DTT; mix.
Cover tube and heat at 95 °C for 15 min on a thermomixer shaking at 300 rpm (or static incubation with gentle mixing every 5 min).
Cool to room temperature (~10 min).
Add 25 µL of 360 mM IAA to reach 40 mM final IAA; incubate in the dark for 30 min.
Add 16.1 µL of 12 % phosphoric acid to reach 1.2 % final concentration; mix.
Add 600 µL freshly prepared S‑Trap binding buffer; mix (solution becomes cloudy).
Place a S‑Trap spin column (cap loosely) into a 2 mL microcentrifuge tube to collect waste.
Load 250 µL of the prepared sample onto the S‑Trap column; centrifuge at 4 000 × g for 30 s.
Repeat loading with 200 µL aliquots, centrifuging after each addition, until the entire sample is loaded (max 100 µg protein per column).
Wash the column three times with 300 µL S‑Trap binding buffer each (centrifuge after each wash).
Transfer the column to a new clean 2 mL tube.
Add 115 µL of 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate (ABC) to the column.
Add 10 µL of trypsin solution (≈1 mg mL⁻¹), cap, and incubate at 37 °C for 18 h.

steps.title: Trypsin digestion (plate format)
steps.instruction: Perform reduction, alkylation, acidification, S‑Trap binding, and overnight digestion using a 96‑well S‑Trap plate.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend each depleted sample in 50 µL of 1× lysis buffer.
Add 5 µL of 110 mM DTT (prepared from powder or 1 M stock) to reach 10 mM final DTT; mix.
Cover the deep‑well plate with a sealing mat and heat at 95 °C for 15 min with shaking/mixing.
Cool to room temperature (~10 min) or centrifuge 2 min.
Add 5 µL of 240 mM IAA (fresh, light‑sensitive) to reach 20 mM final IAA; incubate in the dark for 30 min.
Add 5 µL of 32.5 % phosphoric acid to reach 2.5 % final concentration; mix.
Add 390 µL freshly prepared S‑Trap binding buffer; mix (solution becomes cloudy).
Label the S‑Trap plate and place it on a square‑well collection plate to collect waste.

Add 250 µL of sample to the S‑Trap plate; repeat until all sample is transferred. Apply increasing pressure with a Tecan A200 Positive Pressure Manifold (or centrifuge at 800 × g for 2–5 min) to pass liquid through the membrane.
Wash the plate four times with 300 µL S‑Trap binding buffer, applying positive pressure each time.
Place the S‑Trap plate on a clean 2 mL deep‑well collection plate.

Add 150 µL of 50 mM ABC containing trypsin (minimum 1:50 enzyme:protein ratio; 1:100 may be insufficient). Cover and incubate in a humidified container (e.g., zip‑lock bag with damp Kimwipe or sealed with a clear lid and a pan of water) at 37 °C for 18 h.

steps.title: Peptide elution (tube format)
steps.instruction: Elute digested peptides from the S‑Trap spin column using three sequential buffers.

substeps.instruction: Bring the S‑Trap column rack to room temperature; remove the column cap.
Add 40 µL of elution buffer 1 (50 mM TEAB) to the column and centrifuge at 4 000 × g for 1 min.
Add 40 µL of elution buffer 2 (0.2 % formic acid) and centrifuge at 4 000 × g for 1 min.
Add 40 µL of elution buffer 3 (50 % acetonitrile with 0.2 % formic acid) and centrifuge at 4 000 × g for 1 min.
Pool all eluates, dry down (e.g., SpeedVac), and resuspend in the aqueous buffer (47.5 % ACN, 47.5 % water, 5 % formic acid) for LC‑MS analysis.

steps.title: Peptide elution (plate format)
steps.instruction: Elute peptides from the S‑Trap 96‑well plate using sequential buffers and positive pressure.

substeps.instruction: Allow the S‑Trap plate to reach room temperature; place a collection‑plate spacer between the S‑Trap plate and the collection plate.
Dispense 50 µL of 50 mM ABC (or 50 mM TEAB) onto each well using the Tecan A200 and apply positive pressure.
Add 50 µL of buffer A (99.4 % water, 0.5 % ACN, 0.1 % formic acid) and apply pressure.
Add 50 µL of buffer B (99.9 % ACN, 0.1 % formic acid); let stand ≥5 min, then apply pressure.
Freeze the plate at –80 °C for ≥1 h, then dry in a SpeedVac at –4 °C.
Reconstitute dried peptides in 5 % acetonitrile with 0.1 % formic acid prior to LC‑MS.

steps.title: DIA LC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the peptide samples by data‑independent acquisition on a Vanquish Neo UHPLC coupled to a Thermo Fisher Ascend Tribrid mass spectrometer using the following LC and MS settings: load onto an Acclaim PepMap C18 trap (7 cm total length, 2 cm bed, 3 µm particles, 100 Å pores) and an IonOpticks Aurora Ultimate analytical column (25 cm × 75 µm ID, 1.7 µm particles) at 300 nL min⁻¹ with a 60‑min gradient (5 % B to 30 % B over 50 min, then 95 % B over 5 min, finish at 99 % B for 5 min). Solvent A = water + 0.1 % formic acid; Solvent B = 80 % acetonitrile + 0.1 % formic acid. Perform four “zebra” washes of the trap column and three alternating aqueous/organic washes of the analytical column between samples. MS parameters: spray voltage 2 050 V, charge state 2+, quadrupole isolation for master scan, Orbitrap resolution 120 K (350–1650 m/z), max injection time 100 ms, normalized AGC target 50 %. DIA scan: quadrupole isolation width 20 m/z with 4 m/z overlap (40 scan events), HCD normalized collision energy 28 %, Orbitrap resolution 30 K (360–1160 m/z), max injection time 50 ms, AGC target 1 000 %.
